# Lattice Shuffled Residues

> A theoretical study of histogram correlations in a shuffled lattice-signature observation model, with a fixed-public-matrix theorem, explicit moments and concentration, and a bounded-witness consequence for repeated-view simulation.

## Entry points

- [Project overview](README.md): scientific question, principal results, quantitative scale, reproduction, and scope.
- [Connected scientific account](science/README.md): proof dependencies and the role of each distribution.
- [Learning introduction](learning/README.md): a complete scalar example and a route through the project.
- [Local foundations](learning/FOUNDATIONS.md): finite fields, negacyclic modules, rank and fibers, moments, conditioning, total variation, and bounded witnesses.
- [Selected anchor and bridge](learning/ANCHOR.md): Boneh–Shoup v0.6, verified section pointers, notation, and the material supplied locally.
- [Thirty milestones](learning/MILESTONES.md): the project-defined common map, M01–M10 foundations and M11–M30 scientific narrative.
- [Related work](references/RELATED_WORK.md): closest comparisons, original and corrected source versions, and unresolved full-text overlap checks.
- [Bibliography](references/references.bib): structured primary-source records.

## Questions and authoritative pages

- How should a new reader enter the project? Read the [worked introduction](learning/README.md), use the [single-anchor bridge](learning/ANCHOR.md), and follow the [milestone dependencies](learning/MILESTONES.md). The map organizes the project's understanding targets rather than the book's full contents.
- What information is visible? Read [Model](science/model.md), especially the enlarged view, exact first-check conditioning, and fresh first-attempt strategy.
- Why can an anonymous histogram retain a secret-dependent correlation? Read [Boundary statistic](science/boundary_statistic.md), equations (B1)–(B10).
- Is the public matrix redrawn for each record? No. Read [Fixed public matrix](science/fixed_matrix.md) for a one-time matrix draw and simultaneous control of all translations of one fixed product box.
- Why are only four coordinates needed? Read [Concentration](science/concentration.md): the mean uses two-coordinate marginals and the second moment uses at most four.
- What probability and observation count are proved? Read the theorem and parameter table in [Concentration](science/concentration.md).
- What does public-key simulation imply? Read [Security scope](science/security_scope.md) for any-witness validation, full-key rank exceptions, joint simulation, decision-assumption conditions, exact arithmetic, storage, and signer costs.
- What is wrong with the particular one-transcript replacement? Read [Replacement marginal](science/sampler_marginal.md) for the exact scalar probability gap and its local repair.
- How are calculations reproduced? Read [Verification](verification/README.md), run [check_identities.py](verification/check_identities.py), and compare [results.json](verification/results.json).

## Essential distinctions

The genuine experiment fixes one public matrix and one bounded secret across observations. Independent uniform output coordinates are a comparison law used to calculate moments, not a claim about the full genuine output vector. The specific corrected-SUCRE replacement sampler is a third distribution with a separate scalar discrepancy.

The residual histogram is a complete noiseless observation in an enlarged proof model. The statistical theorem does not supply a physical trace-acquisition argument. The full-key completion uses an uncompressed public relation; compressed verification keys require additional information.

Accepted first-check-passing records retain their centered contribution. Only first-check failures contribute zero by definition. The displayed observation counts are conservative sufficient analytical bounds and are extremely large.

A failed hardness premise and a missing hypothesis in a proof composition have different logical effects. The repeated-view obstruction is conditional on bounded-witness hardness at the simulator's and postprocessor's combined resource budget.

Prior work already combines shuffled information with indexed public data. Attribute that general principle to the sources identified in the related-work account. The project's contribution is its specified residual/high-bit correlation and the theorem that supports repeated observations under one fixed matrix.
